transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I guess what brings me in is that I just always feel like I’m moving from one thing to the next. It's not a huge problem or anything—I just really can’t sit idle, you know? I like to stay productive. 

But, um, we have this new work setup at my job, and... well, it's just made my pacing and fidgeting a lot harder to hide, I suppose. I don't want my supervisors to get the wrong impression of me, since I always try to do a good job. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you often feel restless or find it difficult to sit still for extended periods?

Well, I wouldn't say it's a major problem, really. I just... I like to be doing something, you know? But, um, I guess if I have to sit still through a long training video at work, or if things are just moving really slow... I do start to feel a little boxed in. 

It's not that I can't handle it, it's just... I get this feeling like I really need to stand up, or stretch my legs, or at least be doing something with my hands to stay focused. I'm sure a lot of people get a little antsy during those things, right? Is that what you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn't a clear reason to be concerned?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I worry about the normal stuff, like doing a good job at work or making sure the bills are paid, but... not for no reason. 

Working in customer service all these years, you kind of have to learn to just let things roll off your back, you know? I try to keep a pretty positive attitude. I really don't want to be one of those people who's always stressing and bringing everyone else down. So, I wouldn't say I'm much of a worrier. I hope that's a good thing? Did I answer that the way you needed?
Do you ever find it hard to focus or concentrate on tasks, even when you're trying your best to pay attention?

Well, um... I try really hard to stay on top of things, so I hope it doesn't sound like I'm slacking off. I think my focus is usually pretty good. But, I guess... sometimes, like if we're in one of those longer coaching meetings at work, or if I have to read through a long new procedure... 

I always start off fine. I really do try my best to pay attention. But after a few minutes, I'll kind of realize my eyes just kept moving across the page, or I'm looking right at the manager, and I didn't really take in what was said. I always feel a bit embarrassed when I catch myself doing it, because I really want to do a good job and be respectful. But I figure everyone gets a little zoned out during long meetings sometimes, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee. Does that answer what you were asking?
Outside of work situations like meetings or reading, do you ever have trouble focusing on things at home, like when you're reading a book, watching a movie, or having a conversation with someone?

Well, um... I really try to be present, especially with my wife, because she loves her quiet evenings. I don't want you to think I'm ignoring her or anything like that. But... I guess even with the quiet stuff that's supposed to relax me, like reading a book at home or sitting through a whole movie... it's a little tricky. 

I usually start off fine! But then, I don't know, I just find myself shifting around a lot on the couch, or maybe I'll start making little comments about the movie, or I'll suddenly remember I need to get up and grab a glass of water or check on something in the other room. My wife sometimes gives me a look, and I feel awful because I really do want to just sit and enjoy the movie with her. I just... I guess my brain likes to stay busy, even when I'm supposed to be relaxing. Is that normal for guys my age? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you ever find yourself acting quickly without thinking it through, like interrupting others, making impulsive decisions, or feeling like you just can't wait your turn?

Well, um... I really try to be polite, you know? I've been in customer service a long time, so I know how important it is to let people speak. I definitely don't want to come across as one of those pushy people who just talks over everyone. 

But... I guess sometimes, if I'm at work and I hear some of the other reps struggling with a customer problem... I might just sort of... jump in. Like, I'll hear them trying to figure it out, and I already know the answer, so I'll just kind of blurt it out before they've finished explaining, or before they even ask for my help. 

I always feel a little bad right after, because I don't mean to intrude or be rude. I just want to help them solve it quickly, you know? I'm just trying to be a team player. But I worry sometimes it makes me look like a know-it-all. I really hope my coworkers don't think I'm trying to show them up. Do you think that's just me trying too hard to be helpful? I hope I'm answering these questions the right way for you.
Looking back, did you feel this same sense of restlessness or need to stay busy when you were a child, or is this something that mostly started in adulthood?

Well, um... I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm making excuses for myself, because I've always tried to be a good student and a hard worker. I don't want you to think I've just been slacking my whole life. 

But, I guess... if I'm being really honest... this isn't exactly new. It was around long before my recent job change. Even way back in grade school, I remember... well, my parents kept some of my old report cards, and the teachers would always write things like... "he's a bright boy, but he's careless," or that I talked out of turn a lot. They were always having to remind me to stay with my work and not wander off. 

I always felt so bad when my parents read those notes, because I really was trying to be good. I just... I guess I've always had a little trouble sitting still and keeping quiet when I'm supposed to. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid. I was just energetic, I think. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
Do you ever notice yourself feeling restless or having trouble staying seated in social situations or other structured settings, like church, meetings, or public events?

Well, um... I really try to be respectful in those kinds of places. Like at church, or if there's a speaker, I know how important it is to pay attention. I definitely don't want to be a distraction to anyone else, so I really do my best to sit quietly and be polite. 

But... I guess sometimes, if I'm stuck sitting still through a long training video at work, or maybe a really slow appointment—not this one, of course, you've been wonderful!—I do get a little... well, I start to feel kind of boxed in. It's like my body just decides it needs to stand up, or stretch, or I just need to find something to do with my hands. I'll usually just fiddle with a pen or something small in my lap so no one notices. 

I always try to keep it under wraps because I don't want people to think I'm bored or being disrespectful to whoever is talking. It's just a little extra energy, I think. I hope that makes sense? Am I explaining things clearly enough for you?
Outside of work and structured settings, do you ever find it hard to finish tasks like chores around the house, or do you often lose track of time or forget things easily?

Well, um... I really try to stay on top of things, you know? I want to be reliable, both at home and at work. I've got a system, and I really do my best to keep everything organized. I don't want you to think I'm just letting things fall apart or ignoring my responsibilities.

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes little things do sort of slip through the cracks. Not on purpose, of course! Like, at work, I'll mean to call a customer back, or maybe answer an internal message right after my lunch break. I have every intention of doing it. But... unless I write it down, and I mean, write it down in more than one place... it can just completely slip my mind until the next day. 

I always feel terrible when it happens, because I pride myself on good customer service. I don't want anyone thinking I don't care about their problems. I just get caught up in the next call or the next task, and the time just gets away from me. I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I do eventually get to it! Do you think that's pretty normal for someone my age, or is that the kind of thing you're looking for?
Do you ever find that your restlessness or difficulty focusing affects your personal relationships or causes problems with household responsibilities?

Well, um... as far as things at home go, I really try my absolute best to pull my weight. I don't want my wife to feel like she has to do everything, so I really make an effort to be helpful around the house. I'd hate to be a burden to her. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely open with you... where it's actually been causing a bit of a problem lately is at work. I really hate to admit this, because I want you to know I have a very strong work ethic, but... it's actually started showing up a little bit in my performance reviews. 

My supervisors, they... well, they've had to point out some unfinished tickets, and a couple of mistakes I've made here and there. They mentioned that it can sort of slow the rest of the team down sometimes. I felt just terrible hearing that, because I really am trying so, so hard to do a good job. And I generally get along so well with the customers! People always say I'm very friendly and helpful on the phone. 

I just hate the idea that I might be letting my coworkers down with these little slip-ups. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee. I care a lot about my job. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I brought up work instead of just home life... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.

latest_inference.note: The patient's lifelong history of restlessness, difficulty sitting still, trouble focusing, and impulsive behaviors (e.g., interrupting coworkers), along with functional impairment at work and some impact on personal life, strongly supports a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. Symptoms have been present since childhood and are causing clinically significant impairment in multiple settings. Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F43.0) and Unspecified Anxiety Disorder (F41.9) are ruled out due to the absence of significant worry or anxiety as primary features.
